topic: RU journalists attacked by Chhatra Dal
headline_marked: [[4 journalists injured in Chhatra Dal attack]] at Rajshahi University, 10 total hurt
headline: 4 journalists injured in Chhatra Dal attack at Rajshahi University, 10 total hurt
summary: At least 10 individuals, including four journalists, were injured in a brutal attack by Chhatra Dal activists at Rajshahi University. The incident, sparked by a Facebook post comment, involved local weapons and led to several hospitalizations.
details: At least 10 individuals, including four journalists, were severely injured in a brutal attack by Bangladesh Chhatra Dal (JCD) activists at Rajshahi University (RU). The National Citizen Party (NCP) has strongly condemned the incident, demanding exemplary punishment for those involved.

The violence erupted on Sunday night in front of Shaheed Ziaur Rahman Hall, stemming from an argument over a Facebook post comment. JCD members reportedly gathered with various local weapons, creating a tense atmosphere.

As journalists attempted to cover the situation, they were ambushed by Chhatra Dal activists wielding machetes, hockey sticks, iron pipes, and baseball bats. Four journalists, including representatives from Samakal, The Daily Star, bdnews24.com, and Agamir Somoy, sustained serious injuries.

Journalist Zahidul Islam suffered a severe head injury. Attackers also physically assaulted journalists and threatened to 'bury them alive'. Witnesses identified at least 10 JCD members, including senior leaders, as directly involved.

The injured journalists were initially treated at the university medical center before being transferred to Rajshahi Medical College Hospital (RMCH) due to deteriorating conditions. The NCP expressed outrage over the armed display and terrorist activities by a political student organization on a university campus.

NCP leaders demanded the immediate arrest and exemplary punishment of the identified Chhatra Dal members under strict party and state laws. They also called for the university administration to ensure a safe working environment and full security for general students and media personnel on campus.

headline_marked: [[12kg LPG cylinder price jumps by Tk 252]] to Tk 1,837, adding to consumer woes
headline: 12kg LPG cylinder price jumps by Tk 252 to Tk 1,837, adding to consumer woes
summary: This significant hike comes barely two weeks after transport fuel prices rose, further straining household budgets already grappling with supply shortages and inflated market rates.
details: Household budgets in Bangladesh are facing another significant squeeze as the price of a 12kg LPG cylinder has surged by Tk 252, reaching Tk 1,837. This increase, effective yesterday, follows closely on the heels of a rise in transport fuel prices, adding to the financial burden on consumers.

Despite the official price hike, many households are already paying much more than the regulated rate due to a persistent supply crunch. Retailers in the capital reported not receiving cylinders for days, with available brands being sold at prices up to Tk 2,250, significantly higher than the newly fixed rate.

This situation is not new; on September 30, cylinders were sold for Tk 2,000-2,200 against a regulated price of Tk 1,585. The latest LPG hike also follows a Tk 20 per litre increase in transport fuel prices on September 21, exacerbating the pressure on everyday expenses.

The Bangladesh Energy Regulatory Commission (BERC) attributed the increase to higher international prices of propane and butane, the main components of LPG, and increased shipping costs. The average import cost of these components rose to $712 per tonne from $593 in July, with shipping costs also climbing.

However, local market supply has reportedly fallen since mid-September, with retailers indicating reduced supplies from importers and wholesalers. Industry sources suggest some operators may have reduced market releases, creating an artificial shortage while awaiting BERC's price adjustment.

This shortage and price disparity have already impacted consumption, with monthly demand estimated to have dropped from 1.5 lakh tonnes to 1.3 lakh tonnes as some households switch to alternative cooking methods. BERC reviews LPG prices monthly based on global rates and import costs.

Critics, including Prof M Shamsul Alam of the Consumers Association of Bangladesh, argue that BERC fails to properly examine shipping costs and enforce its own orders, accusing it of protecting unscrupulous businesses. Opposition party Jamaat-e-Islami has condemned the hike, calling for its immediate withdrawal and alleging market control by syndicates.
